extracted.intended_audience: investigative journalists, newsrooms, producers, and students planning to enter the IRE Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for submitting investigative reporting (print, online, audio, video, books, student work, and special categories) to the annual Investigative Reporters & Editors (IRE) Awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantially the product of the reporter’s own initiative and effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries will be judged on whether the work is substantially the product of the reporter’s own initiative and effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a core eligibility/judging criterion emphasizing original initiative and effort by the credited reporter(s). Student categories have additional rules about faculty roles (instructional, editing, fact-checking, mentoring) that still permit eligibility provided the students did the reporting, data analysis, interviews and writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncovers facts someone or some agency may have tried to keep from public scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should uncover facts that someone or some agency may have tried to keep from public scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion stresses investigative impact and originality — reporting that reveals concealed or obscured information.

rubrics_metrics.name: About issues of public importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Be about issues of public importance to the readers, viewers or listeners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should address matters that matter to the public audience the entry serves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shows enterprise and excellence in documentation, data, storytelling, production, online presentation, and reader or viewer involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows enterprise and excellence in documentation, data, storytelling, production, online presentation, and reader or viewer involvement where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges evaluate both the reporting methods and the quality of presentation across formats (text, audio, video, online interactivity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: All work must have been published or aired between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31 of the award year (for 2025 awards, published/aired between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries that include significant investigative findings previously published or aired during a prior year are subject to unfavorable judging unless accompanied by a detailed explanation of which findings are new and why it was necessary to include previous work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership requirement (entrants)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one journalist named in the story's or series' byline must be a current IRE member. For the 2025 awards, that membership must be current through June 30, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries with no current members listed will be disqualified. You must enter the current member’s expiration date (day, month, year) to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest questionnaire and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must include a filled-out contest questionnaire saved as a PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges may disqualify any entry with an incomplete questionnaire. Save and upload your questionnaire as required; failure to include required materials risks disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest / judge & committee eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that included any significant role by an IRE contest judge may not be entered; Contest Committee members are not eligible to enter; Executive Committee members (including Board Chair) are also not allowed to enter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlets can enter work that includes editing/oversight by a committee member so long as the committee member did not make contributions that would merit a byline or another prominent role. If a potential conflict arises, the committee member must discuss with the committee chair and recuse if warranted; unresolved issues go to the Executive Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries may be disqualified for incomplete questionnaires, failure to disclose known challenges to accuracy or fairness, inclusion of ads in video/audio entries, or disregarding other rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to disclose accuracy/fairness issues can result in disqualification or other penalties. Any ads left in media entries will result in disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size definitions and entry fees (print/online & video)
rubrics_metrics.description: Size categories define which entry-class you use: INTERNATIONAL, NATIONAL, REGIONAL/LARGE MARKET, STATE/MEDIUM MARKET, LOCAL/SMALL MARKET — each with precise circulation/market-size criteria and associated entry fees ($100, $80, $60, $40 depending on size and category).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For partnerships/collaborations, enter the largest organization involved. For online-only news organizations, magazines and weeklies, size is determined by primary coverage area. Exact circulation and DMA ranges are specified on the page; fees vary by category and size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio category size & fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio categories use LARGE (national and regional news organizations) and SMALL (state and local news organizations) sizing with entry fees ($100 large; $60 small).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audio size definitions follow the Print/Online specifications for national/regional vs. state/local equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student authorship requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Student entries must be original investigative reports where reporting, data analysis, interviews and writing are the work of the students; professors/faculty may serve in instructional, editor, fact-checking, or mentoring roles but may not contribute reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If published or broadcast by a professional organization, the professional outlet must have contributed no reporting and the editorial process must be transparently described in a mandatory disclosure statement included with the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student category size definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Student categories: Individual (one student), Small Team (2–5 students), Large Team (6 or more students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story ideas for Individual entries must have originated with the student; solo entries whose idea originated with a professor should enter Small Team instead. There is also a 'Best of Class for Exceptional Enterprise' student category with special submission allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory disclosure for student entries
rubrics_metrics.description: All student entries must include a statement describing how the work was conceived, reported, edited, and (if applicable) published or aired—including any contributions made by others for production or distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosure should explain the educational context, how students developed/took ownership of the reporting if topics were suggested by faculty, and detail any stylistic/technical adjustments or professional contributions if published by a professional outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary material limits — print/online
rubrics_metrics.description: For print/online categories: one story in a series counts as one piece of primary material; entrants are limited to five primary stories/elements (select the best five).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may include one additional link and/or PDF as supplemental material. Supplemental material might include audio/video used elsewhere, follow-up stories, editorials, or elements outside the five-story limit. Each file upload max = 3MB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary material limits — audio & video
rubrics_metrics.description: For audio/video categories: the first 30 minutes of submitted audio/video is considered primary material; for series, the best 30 minutes can be compiled or you can submit up to five pieces not exceeding 30 minutes total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must include a transcript of your primary stories. You may include one additional link and/or PDF as supplemental material. Each file upload max = 3MB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercials and underwriting removal (audio/video)
rubrics_metrics.description: All commercials, underwriting credits, sponsors, bumps, teasers, or any non-editorial ads must be removed from audio and video entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes preroll, midroll, postroll and any show opens that mention funders or advertising. Any ads left in will result in disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries in languages other than English are accepted only if accompanied by translations; video entries in other languages should include a translated script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcripts of primary material should be included (PDF). Ensure translations/scripts accurately reflect the submitted material for judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Books (book category) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Book submissions must be for outstanding investigative reporting that resulted in a published book; only eBooks are accepted for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a link or a PDF ready; fill out the contest questionnaire and save as a PDF. Entry fee for books and special categories is $75.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special category criteria and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Special categories include Tom Renner Award (best investigative reporting on organized crime/other criminal acts; limited to 10 stories), IRE FOI Award (honors actions that further open records/open government), Investigations Triggered by Breaking News (work done within 30 days of an event), IRE Award for Sports Investigations, and Longform Journalism (audio/video).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to platform-specific rules for required entry material. Longform audio/video are projects primarily presented in >30 minutes of work with no time limit on submissions for that category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental material rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants may include one additional link and/or PDF as supplemental material beyond the primary material limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental material can include audio/video used elsewhere, follow-up stories, editorials, or elements outside the primary limits. Supplemental cover letter to judges is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: File upload size and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each file upload has a maximum file size of 3MB; transcripts and contest questionnaire must be saved as PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PDFs and uploaded files meet the size limit and include any necessary login credentials for links behind paywalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of entries allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit to the number of entries a person or outlet may submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry fees apply per entry and are non-refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process and possible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each category is reviewed by screeners; screened entries move to the IRE Awards Committee which determines finalists, winners, and medalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the judges’ discretion, they may give no award or award multiple entries in a given category. The top award is the IRE Medal; other winning entries receive an IRE award.
